summary: Taixu (1890–1947) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Jing'an, Jichan, and Renshan Yang at Jinling Scriptural Press. He served at Bilu Temple and as leader of Minnan Buddhist Institute, which he founded.

Taizan Maezumi (1931–1995) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Komazawa University, Sōji-ji, San Francisco State University, and under Hakujun Kuroda, Koryu Osaka, and Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani. In 1956, he became a priest at Zenshuji Soto Mission.
Tak Pui Sze is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies who earned a PhD at the University of British Columbia, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Jinhua Chen (attested 2012).

Taka Yanagisawa (1926–2003) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Japan Women's University (~1943–1947) and served as Director of the Department of Fine Arts at the Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties (~1952–1989).
Takahiko Kameyama is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts as a professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University, both attested in 2015.
Takahiko Sato (born 1944) is a scholar in Buddhist studies who served as a professor at Koyasan University, attested in 2015 and 2026.

Takahiro Asano works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and other fields, holding degrees from Chiba, Doshisha, Washington, and York universities. He held posts at Kyoto International Social Welfare Exchange Centre, Japan Lutheran College, and Musashino University.

Takahiro Kato (born 1974) is a scholar of Indology and philosophy holding a Dr.Phil from Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg. As of 2026, he is a professor at the University of Tokyo and affiliated with the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.
Takako Abe is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer (attested 2013–2017) and faculty member (attested 2026) at Taisho University.

Takamaro Shigaraki (1926–2014) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University, University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and Institute of Buddhist Studies. At Ryukoku, he served on the faculty, as professor, and as president (1989–1995).

Takamatsu Yoshie (1880–1940) studied at Matsumoto Fukashi High School, Tōkyō Senmon Gakkō, Waseda University, and the University of Paris. He taught English at Waseda Junior and Senior High School, lectured at Waseda University, and became its Dean of Literature (1930).

Takami Inoue is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. Inoue was a doctoral candidate at the University of California, Santa Barbara (attested 2003) and served as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies at Otani University.

Takamichi Fukita is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Taisho and Bukkyo universities under Zenno Ishigami, Shozen Kumoi, Yuichi Kajiyama, and Heinz Bechert, and later held a lectureship at Bukkyo University (attested 1999, 2013).

Takanobu Takahashi (born 1951) is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Tokyo, Madurai Kamaraj University under Tamilannal, and Utrecht University, later serving on the faculty at Shitennoji University and the University of Tokyo.

Takanori Fukita is a scholar of Buddhist studies who was a graduate student at Bukkyo University (attested 2017) and served as a specially appointed lecturer at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

Takanori Shintani (born 1948) is a scholar of religious studies and Japanology. He studied at Waseda University (~1968–1977) and held academic posts at the Graduate University for Advanced Studies (~1996–2010) and Kokugakuin University (~2010–2019).

Takanori Unno (born 1936) is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his doctoral studies at Nagoya University. He held academic posts at Nagoya University, Aichi Prefectural University of Fine Arts and Music, and Meijo University.

Takao Hayashi (born 1949) is an Indologist and historian. He earned degrees from Tohoku, Kyoto, and Brown universities, studying under David Pingree. His posts include Harish-Chandra Research Institute, Kyoto Women's University, and assistant professor and professor at Doshisha University.
Takao Kagawa (born 1926) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Susumu Yamaguchi, Issai Funahashi, and Shoju Inaba, and served as a professor at Bukkyo University.

Takao Maruyama (born 1929) is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral coursework at Tohoku University in 1962. He held professorships at Rissho University, Shinshu University (where he became professor emeritus), and Mejiro University.
